skill.name: set-up-lightspeed-meta-new-customer-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to check Lightspeed eCom tracking and set up a Meta conversion based on revenue or profit from each customer's first paid order.
skill.summary: Set up and verify first-order conversion tracking for Meta Ads on Lightspeed eCom.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts match Markdown, vendor documentation, or routine authenticated setup. The unpinned installer and gaps in credential handling, browser handoffs, live tracking approval, and profit event selection warrant fixes. No evidence of prompt injection or covert exfiltration was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The assistant may request credentials and pass them to a command.
remediation.suggestion: Require the verified vendor interface or a dedicated secret input. Remove instructions to request credentials in conversation or include them in command arguments.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not explicitly require approval before enabling live Meta delivery.
remediation.suggestion: Show the workspace, store, pixel, consent rules, and transmitted data. Require approval before enabling live delivery or removing the test code.

remediation.issue: Tool-provided browser URLs are forwarded without destination verification.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the HTTPS origin against the expected provider for each setup step. Do not forward URLs that fail verification.

remediation.issue: The optional installer does not pin its package or skill source.
remediation.suggestion: Document installation using a verified installer version and a reviewed, immutable source revision. Require explicit user approval before execution.

remediation.issue: The main workflow cites an all-order profit event for new customer bidding.
remediation.suggestion: Use PMNewCustomerProfit with CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT consistently for first-order profit. Verify the rule and event in Events Manager before proposing a campaign change.

semantic_findings.title: Assistant Credential Handling Conflicts With App-Only Entry
semantic_findings.description: The skill permits requesting store secrets and Meta tokens from the user and passing them to a command. This can expose credentials in transcripts, tool logs, or process arguments. The setup references also direct entry in the app.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception explicitly permits the assistant to request credentials and pass them to a command. It specifies no protected input channel.

semantic_findings.title: Live Meta Delivery Lacks a Separate Approval Check
semantic_findings.description: The guide leaves Meta sending enabled and later removes the test code. It does not require a separate review of the destination, consent settings, and matching data before production delivery.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The references identify the live transition and matching data, but the explicit human checkpoint concerns campaign selection. The integration does document shopper consent.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Handoffs Do Not Verify the Destination
semantic_findings.description: The assistant relays a tool-provided URL for the user to open without checking its origin. A wrong or tampered URL could misdirect a user during account setup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly relays the returned URL, and account setup includes provider authorization. No malicious URL or compromised response was observed.

semantic_findings.title: Profit Event Conflicts With the New Customer Goal
semantic_findings.description: The main skill names the general profit event for this goal, while the dedicated guide names the first-order profit event. Following the main instruction can optimize spending for repeat purchases instead of new customer acquisition.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The main skill specifies PMOrderProfit with ORDER_PROFIT. The dedicated workflow specifies PMNewCustomerProfit with CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT instead.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta New Customer Bidding for Lightspeed
content.value_statement: Standard purchase conversions count sales from both first-time and repeat buyers. Use first-order revenue or profit from Lightspeed to give Meta a separate signal for new customer acquisition.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status and identify missing store, tracking, or Meta connections.
Check recent Lightspeed orders for new, returning, or unknown customer classifications.
Guide a paid test order and verify first-order event delivery in Meta Events Manager.
Explain the event and custom conversion rule for first-order revenue or profit.
Show the campaign setting the operator changes and summarize what remains unverified.
limitations: Requires a Lightspeed eCom C-Series store, Product Metrics Pro, and a Cloudflare storefront gateway.
The operator creates the custom conversion and selects it in Meta. The assistant does not make those changes.
Profit events require complete cost data. Orders without a matched customer do not qualify for new customer events.
Historical orders are not imported, and later refunds do not revise first-order events already sent to Meta.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Confirm the store, gateway, consent banner, and Meta destination before testing any first-order event.

use_cases.title: Validate First-Order Tracking
use_cases.description: Check a paid test order and confirm that Meta receives the revenue event with the correct conversion rule.

use_cases.title: Prepare a First-Order Profit Pilot
use_cases.description: Review margin data and first-order profit delivery before changing the optimization event in one campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Review an existing Lightspeed store.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my Lightspeed store is ready for Meta new customer bidding. List missing steps without changing settings or asking for credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recent Order Classifications
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Check how Lightspeed classifies buyers.
prompt_templates.prompt: For my selected store, count how many of the last 20 orders were new, returning, or unknown. Do not include customer identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Revenue Test Event
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Validate tracking before enabling live delivery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a paid test order with marketing and analytics consent. Help me verify the first-order revenue event in Meta Test Events.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Profit Pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Evaluate first-order profitability before a campaign change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check margin readiness and verify the first-order profit event and rule. Give me the steps for one ad set without changing the campaign.

output_examples.input: Check whether my store is ready for a first-order revenue test.
output: Store connection: Active. Storefront gateway: Complete.
Meta destination: Saved. Test event delivery: Not yet verified.
Next step: Place a paid test order as a first-time buyer with marketing and analytics consent.

output_examples.input: Review the last 20 orders and tell me whether first-order profit is ready.
output: Order classifications: 8 new, 10 returning, and 2 unknown.
Profit is not ready because margin data is incomplete. Complete the cost setup and verify a first-order profit test event before changing the ad set.

best_practices: Enter API credentials in the verified vendor app, not in chat.
Verify the intended pixel, consent settings, and test event before enabling live delivery.
Test the first-order conversion in one campaign before rolling it out to other campaigns.
anti_patterns: Selecting the all-order profit event when the goal is first-order profit.
Assuming an order with unknown customer status is a first purchase.
Leaving a test event code active and expecting events to appear in live reporting.

faq.question: Which Lightspeed stores does this support?
faq.answer: It supports Lightspeed eCom C-Series stores in the European and US regions. You also need Product Metrics Pro and a proxied Cloudflare storefront domain.

faq.question: How does Product Metrics recognize a new customer?
faq.answer: It checks Lightspeed's new-customer flag and order history. The classification may remain unknown while history is checked.

faq.question: Can I optimize for first-order profit?
faq.answer: Yes. With complete margin data, create a Meta custom conversion on PMNewCustomerProfit and set the purpose rule to CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT.

faq.question: Why is the first-order event missing in Meta?
faq.answer: Meta lists the event after receiving it once. Place a paid test order as a first-time buyer with marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: Can the assistant change which event my campaign uses?
faq.answer: No. The assistant guides setup and validation. You create the custom conversion in Events Manager and select it for the ad set.

faq.question: Do old orders or later refunds change the conversion?
faq.answer: No. The integration does not import historical orders, and later refunds do not revise first-order conversion events already sent to Meta.
